purpose: Separate design-variable coupling from NL row/column ordering sensitivity in the M5/Bakken tax-zero modernization failure.

experiments.interpretation: Even one free process design variable can trigger the ill-conditioned state solve; coupling among all eight design variables is not required for failure.
Symbol ordering keeps the one-DOF solve feasible and near the archived full optimum but needs more iterations for an accepted termination.
Deterministic symbol ordering converts the modern one-DOF case from failure to an accepted IPOPT optimum; it is not expected to equal the eight-DOF paper result because seven decisions remain fixed.
Ordering materially improves the first step but is not sufficient for the complete modern optimization.
Candidate A1 remains convergent and reproduces the archived result under the same high-level deterministic-order request.

conclusions: The modern failure is present with only one free design variable, so it is rooted in the ill-conditioned state equations rather than requiring eight-way design-variable coupling.
NL ordering materially changes the modern numerical path and can recover the one-DOF solve.
The same sort-symbols request does not make the full Candidate A1 and modern solver outcomes agree, so the high-level determinism setting is not a complete cross-version ordering control.
The next control must compare the actual emitted NL row/column symbol maps and writer grouping across Pyomo 6.4.2 and 6.10.1.
